conclusion: Two concurrent drivers never lost or duplicated a row on this storage. Both safe outcomes were observed: a conflicting writer either committed cleanly or failed with a named Delta exception. This describes Delta 4.2.0 over Docker named volumes on one host and is not evidence for object storage.
method: Two Spark drivers in different containers write to one Delta table on the shared volume. Each materialises its rows, waits on a file barrier so the commits overlap, then writes through the same code path the contracted build uses, including the txnAppId/txnVersion idempotent-write marker. A third read-only pass measures the table afterwards.
not_demonstrated: object storage or any cloud filesystem
concurrent DELETE against a concurrent append

runtime.storage: Docker named volume mounted at /opt/fareline/output in every container

scenarios.name: empty_directory_distinct_versions
scenarios.question: What happens when two drivers create the same table at once?

writers.detail: DELTA_PROTOCOL_CHANGED: the protocol version was changed by a concurrent update, which happens when multiple writers write into an empty directory

scenarios.reading: The loser failed loudly instead of writing a second table state. Creating the table before concurrent writers start avoids the conflict.

scenarios.name: existing_table_distinct_versions
scenarios.question: Can two drivers append two different source versions at the same time?
scenarios.reading: Both commits landed and every row of every version is present exactly once. Appends of disjoint source versions do not conflict.

scenarios.name: existing_table_same_version
scenarios.question: Can a duplicated driver publish the same source version twice?

writers.detail: DELTA_CONCURRENT_TRANSACTION: the transaction identifier was already used by another writer

scenarios.reading: The idempotent-write marker made the duplicate impossible at the transaction-log level, not by a read-side check that two drivers could both pass.
